rationale: M18 (PEReference round). A parameter entity reference is a USE, and all 24 corpus sites were producing no edge. `%defroot;` is how a DTD pulls in another DTD — the same fact `entity_external_id` already records for `<!ENTITY % pe SYSTEM "common.dtd">`, reached by reference instead of by ExternalID, and recorded only for the ExternalID form. The owner is the DOCTYPE'S OWN NAME, because a parameter reference in the internal subset has no element above it: the X7 shape, a claim the document makes dropped for want of anywhere to attach it. Three shapes, and the third is here because its discriminator from the second is ONE CHARACTER. Shape 1 is a parameter reference in the internal subset. Shape 2 is `%name;` inside an entity's replacement text, owned by the DECLARING ENTITY. Shape 3 is `% name 'replacement'` — the parameter-entity VALUE form, which names nothing and must produce no edge; libxml2's corpus holds both `%xx;` and `% zz '<'`, and a rule accepting either would invent names out of literal percent signs. The replacement-text shape is written the way `result/valid/index.xml` writes it, because a first draft butted the reference against markup, which the grammar parses under an ERROR — and pinning an owner for a node the parser could not read would be pinning a fiction.

expectRelationships.note: Shape 2: the owner is the DECLARING ENTITY, not the DOCTYPE and not an element — `outer` cannot be expanded without `inner`. The first version asked the PEReference node itself for an `EntityValue` CHILD, which a reference never has, so the test was always false and libxml2's index.xml published `NewsML -> global-attributes` when the owner should have been the entity using it.
Shape 1: owner is the DOCTYPE's own name, because this reference sits in the internal subset with no element above it.

An undeclared parameter entity is RECORDED and labelled rather than refused — the same ruling as X13 for a bare type reference, and the same reason: refusing it is what makes the claim invisible. There is no builtin form for a parameter entity (there is no `%lt;`), so the answer is binary and copying EntityRef's three-way label here would be a fiction.

forbidRelationships.note: Shape 3: `% zz '<'` is the parameter-entity VALUE form and names nothing. The corpus contains it beside real references precisely so that a rule accepting any `%…;` would be caught — the semicolon is the discriminator.

forbidSymbols.name: zz
forbidSymbols.note: the value form's first token is not a parameter entity name, so nothing may be published for it.

forbidSymbols.name: neverDeclared
forbidSymbols.note: a USE is not a DECLARATION: the reference is recorded, the target symbol is not.
